figures.shows: Graphical tensor-network diagrams of (a) the TT decomposition (a chain of factors linked only to adjacent factors, ranks R1 to R_{N-1}), (b) the TR decomposition (a ring, adding a link between the first and last factors), and (c) the FCTN decomposition (N factors G1..GN, each pair linked by an edge R_{k1,k2}, so fully connected).

papers.what_it_is: A classical (non-quantum) tensor-network paper that proposes the fully-connected tensor network (FCTN) decomposition, builds a proximal-alternating-minimization tensor-completion algorithm on it, states a convergence theorem, and compares it with other tensor-decomposition completion methods on synthetic, video and traffic data.

assertions.value: The paper defines the FCTN decomposition as decomposing an N th-order tensor into a set of N th-order factor tensors, where any two factors share an equal-sized mode used for tensor contraction.
quotes: The FCTN decomposition aims to decompose an N th-order tensor
into a set of N th-order factor tensors
have an equal-sized mode Rk1,k2 used to conduct the tensor contraction operation
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own definition of the object its results depend on.

assertions.value: The authors state that for second-order tensors the FCTN decomposition is actually the matrix factorization and the FCTN-rank is actually the matrix rank.
quotes: for second-order tensors, the FCTN decomposition is
actually the matrix factorization and the FCTN-rank is ac-
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated as an observation without a proof in the text.
assertions.reader_inference: This is a special case that follows from the definition.

assertions.value: The authors state that the FCTN decomposition can degenerate to the TT and TR decompositions by setting the corresponding modes of factors to 1.
quotes: the FCTN decomposition can degenerate to the TT and TR decompositions by simply setting the corresponding modes of factors to 1
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated without a worked proof in the text.

assertions.value: The paper states a theorem (Transpositional Invariance): if an N th-order tensor has an FCTN decomposition, then its generalized transposition (any reordering of the modes) has an FCTN decomposition with correspondingly permuted factors; the authors say the FCTN decomposition is essentially invariable no matter how the modes are permuted.
quotes: Supposing that an N th-order tensor X has the following FCTN decomposition
is essentially invariable, no matter how to permute the modes of the target tensor
assertions.certainty_reason: The statement is quoted, but the file shows no proof of it (the proofs the paper mentions are in the supplement, which was not available).
assertions.reader_inference: The invariance applies to the decomposition form; the empirical test is the synthetic experiment.

assertions.value: The authors state that TT decomposition keeps the invariance only under a reverse permutation of the tensor modes, and TR decomposition only under a circular shift or a reverse permutation.
quotes: keeps the invariance only when the modes of the target tensor make a reverse permuting
TR decomposition keeps the invariance only when the modes of the target tensor make a circular shifting or a reverse permuting
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated as a background claim without proof or citation in the paper.

assertions.value: The paper states a theorem that the FCTN-ranks bound the rank of all generalized tensor unfoldings: the rank of each unfolding is at most a product of the FCTN-ranks between the two groups of modes, with R_{ni,nj} = R_{nj,ni} when ni > nj.
quotes: The following theorem presents that the FCTN-ranks can bound the rank of all generalized tensor unfolding.
where Rni,nj = Rnj,ni if ni > nj
assertions.certainty_reason: Statement quoted, but the bound's inequality is garbled in the text layer and no proof is shown in the file.

assertions.value: The authors state that for an N th-order tensor with all FCTN-ranks equal to R1 the FCTN decomposition requires O(N IR1N−1) parameters, and that the Tucker decomposition requires O(N IR2 + R2N ) parameters.
quotes: the FCTN decomposition requires O(N IR1N−1) parameters to express it
the Tucker decomposition (O(N IR2 + R2N ) parameters)
assertions.certainty_reason: Parameter counts are stated without derivation in the text.

assertions.value: The authors argue that for real-world data the required FCTN-rank R1 is usually far less than the Tucker-rank R2, so the FCTN decomposition is superior to the Tucker decomposition regarding storage cost; they defer more experimental evidence to supplementary material.
quotes: rank R1 is usually far less than Tucker-rank R2
More experimental evidence is provided in the supplementary material
assertions.certainty_reason: An author argument; the supporting experiments are not in the paper.
assertions.reader_inference: The paper itself says FCTN factors are N th-order, so storage is higher than for TT and TR.

assertions.value: The authors state that making all factors N th-order inevitably increases the storage cost compared with the TT and TR decompositions.

to be designed as N th-order tensors, which inevitably leads

assertions.value: The paper states a theorem relating one FCTN factor to the composition of the other factors, which it uses to compute a factor while fixing the others.
quotes: Theorem 4 reveals the relationship between one FCTN
since computing one factor usually needs to ﬁx the others

assertions.value: The proposed FCTN decomposition-based tensor completion (FCTN-TC) model minimizes a squared Frobenius-norm misfit between the tensor and its FCTN composition plus an indicator enforcing agreement with the observed entries.
quotes: the proposed FCTN decomposition-based TC (FCTN-TC) model can be formulated as
Here Ω denotes the index of the known elements
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own model definition.

assertions.value: The paper's PAM-based solver for FCTN-TC uses proximal parameter ρ = 0.1, a maximum of 1000 iterations, and stops when the relative change of the tensor falls below 10−5.
quotes: smax = 1000
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own algorithm settings.

assertions.value: The authors state that each update of a factor involves the FCTN composition, matrix multiplication and matrix inversion, and give a per-iteration computational complexity for Algorithm 1 in terms of N, I and R.
quotes: updating Gk involves the FCTN composition,
the matrix multiplication, and the matrix inversion
assertions.certainty_reason: Complexity expression is garbled in the text layer; the derivation is only sketched.

assertions.value: The authors acknowledge that the computational complexity of the FCTN-TC method is theoretically higher than that of the compared decomposition-based methods.
quotes: although the computational complexity of the FCTN-TC method is theoretically higher
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state this limit of their own method.

assertions.value: The paper states that the sequence obtained by Algorithm 1 globally converges to a critical point of the FCTN-TC problem, to be proved by verifying four conditions of a cited framework (boundedness, proper lower semi-continuity, the K-Ł property, and sufficient decrease plus relative error lemmas).
quotes: obtained by the Algorithm 1 globally converges to a critical point of (2).
we only need to justify that the following four conditions hold
The detailed proof for the above four conditions is presented in the supplementary materials.
assertions.certainty_reason: The statement is quoted but the proof is deferred to supplementary materials not in the file.
assertions.reader_inference: The theorem rests on the cited proximal alternating minimization framework; the file contains only the lemma statements.

assertions.value: Each synthetic tensor is tested in two orderings: the original and one generalized transposition with n = (2, 4, 1, 3) for the fourth-order and (2, 4, 1, 3, 5) for the fifth-order tensor; the random-sampling missing mask and RSE are used, and results are averaged over 50 independent tests.

assertions.value: The authors report that on the synthetic data FCTN-TC is robust to different permutations while TT-TC and TR-TC are sensitive, and that FCTN-TC always achieves the lowest RSE among the three methods across datasets, MRs and permutations.

assertions.reader_inference: The synthetic data are TT-generated and only two tensor sizes and one alternative permutation were tested, so the evidence is narrow.
